A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COMPFLOW research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, appendices and checklists are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original MuJoCo experiments, ablations and wildlife-conservation simulations in Section 5, plus severe-shift experiments in Appendix J.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental and simulation results, including the additional severe-shift results in Appendix J.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 changes the conditioning pairs for offline-generated samples from Doff to Don and corrects OT-pair indexing. Algorithm 4 replaces separately averaged critic losses with a combined-batch mean, moves lambda from the SAC term to the behavior-cloning term, and changes the actor update to gradient descent. These materially revise the documented training procedure; the PDFs do not establish whether implementations or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both retain the same three locomotion environments, three dynamics-shift types and three D4RL dataset qualities, the six extreme-shift settings in Appendix J, and the Murchison Falls-to-Queen Elizabeth wildlife scenario.

E2.justification: SAC, BC-SAC, H2O, BC-VGDF and BC-PAR remain the comparators in Tables 1–2 and Figure 6. The direct-flow comparator in Figure 3 is also retained.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation protocols remain unchanged, including 40K interactions and 400K gradient updates, the 10% dynamics-validation split, hyperparameter sweeps and wildlife interaction budget. The algorithmic revisions are distinct from these retained evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Both contain the same direct-versus-composite-flow analysis, data-selection-ratio sensitivity study, exploration-strength study and extreme-dynamics-shift tests. The added wildlife photographs do not introduce another case study or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both report standard deviations across random seeds in checklist item 7 and retain the same uncertainty displays. No run-count information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–2 and the plotted results in Figures 3–6 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains average returns of 2193 for COMPFLOW and 1920 for BC-SAC; the wildlife discussion retains the 8.8% advantage over BC-PAR.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.3 now explicitly requires matched conditioning marginals. Appendix I substantially replaces the earlier proof with joint-measure definitions, integrability assumptions, conditional-OT decomposition, limiting-coupling arguments and ordered convergence limits. Section 2.3 also replaces an exact learned-transport-cost equality with an approximation. The other principal theorems and proofs are retained, allowing for renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: composite-flow dynamics modeling, Wasserstein gap estimation, improved generalization and exploration of high-gap regions. Their empirical scope and principal performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Remark 3.4 and the new Appendix I intuition explain why mismatched state-action marginals prevent transport from becoming purely conditional, even with a large conditioning penalty, and how sampling from Don addresses this. Existing empirical interpretations and Appendix A limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: The pseudocode now explicitly specifies normalized OT coupling probabilities, categorical pair sampling, selected-batch cardinality and previously implicit algorithm inputs. Code-access statements, hyperparameter tables, simulator details, hardware and runtime disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Santambrogio's Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians and Villani's Optimal Transport: Old and New to support Appendix I. The substantive positioning relative to prior RL methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the abstract, introductory examples, main-results discussion, wildlife narrative and all four pseudocode descriptions. Appendix I is reorganized into a formal proposition, a stepwise proof and an intuition discussion, although the main section order remains intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the wildlife photograph panel in Figure 7 and a boxed intuition discussion, and reformats the algorithm blocks. Existing figures and tables retain their designs, with local changes to placement and surrounding page layout.

improvement.justification: The explicit shared-marginal requirement and corresponding sampling construction address a concrete omission in the estimator's justification. Corrected OT indexing and actor-update direction also improve the pseudocode's coherence. These support a limited quality gain, but unexplained loss reweighting in Algorithm 4 leaves its connection to the unchanged experimental results unresolved.
